Put your own videos on the macOS lock screen.

**Requirements:** macOS 26 (Tahoe), Apple Silicon or Intel, and at least one aerial wallpaper downloaded in System Settings → Wallpaper.

### Install

1. Download **Aerial.Manager_{{version}}_universal.dmg** below, open it, and drag Aerial Manager onto Applications.
2. Open the app. macOS blocks it because it isn't signed yet — click **Done**.
3. Go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, click **Open Anyway** next to "Aerial Manager was blocked", and confirm with Touch ID or your password. You only do this once.
4. Pick your video folders, click **Replace Lock Screen**, choose a video, and lock your screen (Ctrl+Cmd+Q).

Step-by-step with screenshots, troubleshooting and uninstall: [README](https://github.com/kimmjen/aerial-manager#install).

**Coming from the old web version?** Install the app, then in Settings use **Import slots.json** (from the web app's `data/slots.json`) and **Remove old helper**. You no longer need to run `npm run dev`.
